node: Broadline distributors and contracted restaurant procurement
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expands the direct public-company universe for the restaurant broadline-distribution/procurement node. The cleanest reference exposures are Sysco, US Foods, and Performance Food Group: scaled foodservice distributors whose networks can influence restaurant input availability, delivery reliability, private-label penetration, and purchasing economics. The underfollowed discovery candidate is GEN Restaurant Group, not because it owns the distribution chokepoint, but because its filings reveal unusually high supplier concentration: Sysco represented about 76.3% of total food costs in 2024 after a three-year purchase agreement, making procurement terms a potentially material margin and operating-risk variable. No trading recommendation is implied. Expanded the universe around broadline foodservice distribution and contracted restaurant procurement. The two-lane structure separates obvious reference distributors, which define the node economics, from underfollowed restaurant operators and input suppliers where procurement dependency may create hidden margin risk or second-order upside. Strongest direct node anchors are Sysco and US Foods. More underfollowed discovery candidates are GEN Restaurant Group, because filings reportedly disclose a material Sysco agreement and prior US Foods concentration, and Lamb Weston, because restaurant chains appear operationally dependent on consistent frozen-potato supply even where relationships are not purely contractual.
